newsitem.title: CHINA: China congratulates Clinton, eyes more progress.
newsitem.headline: China congratulates Clinton, eyes more progress.

text.p: China congratulated U.S. President Bill Clinton on his re-election on Wednesday and said it was ready to work with the United States for further progress.

"We wish to congratulate President Clinton on his re-election ... Now, a good opportunity has presented itself for improving and expanding Sino-U.S. relations," Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told reporters.
"We are ready to work with the U.S. side for further progress on the basis of the three joint communiques," Cui said.

The communiques were reached between the U.S. and China as part of the rapprochement which began in the early 1970s and led to diplomatic ties in 1979 when Washington dropped its long-time recognition of Taiwan.

On Tuesday, China said the United States had broken its pledge under one of the three communiques -- made in 1982 -- to reduce the quality and quantity of arms sales to Taiwan, which Beijing considers a rebel province.
Cui said said China cherished its friendship with the United States.
"We have all along adopted a positive approach towards Sino-U.S. relations and made unremitting efforts for their development," the spokesman said.
"Recently, thanks to joint efforts from both sides, some positive progress has been made in the bilateral relations with somewhat improved atmosphere," he said.
Sino-U.S. relations have been strained in recent years by disputes over human rights, trade, Taiwan and arms sales and alleged nuclear proliferation.
On Tuesday, U.S. Undersecretary of State Lynn Davis said in Beijing she was encouraged by Chinese efforts to control exports to unsafeguarded nuclear facilities after talks on arms proliferation.
Davis was in China as part of an effort to pave the way for a visit by U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher later this month.
